title: Provisions for filing Return of Income and Self Assessment
outcomes: Identify who must file a return and the due date for each class of assessee.
Apply the rules for belated, revised, defective and updated returns.
Compute interest and fee for late filing and the additional tax on an updated return.
Identify verification, tax return preparer, PAN and Aadhaar requirements.

meta.exam_tip: Write the due date first; every other answer — fee, interest, revision window — flows from it.

concepts.title: Who must file and by when (s. 263(1))
body: A return is the prescribed statement in which a person reports total income, tax, taxes paid and other details for a tax year.

Always required: companies, firms, specified universities and institutions, and a resident and ordinarily resident person who holds, has signing authority over, or benefits from any asset or account outside India — even with a loss or nil income.

Others must file if total income, before Chapter VIII deductions and capital-gain deductions under sections 82–86, exceeds the basic exemption limit (₹4,00,000 under the default regime; ₹2,50,000, ₹3,00,000 or ₹5,00,000 under the optional regime), or if a Rule 163 condition is met: current-account deposits above ₹1 crore; foreign travel spending above ₹2 lakh; electricity bills above ₹1 lakh; business turnover above ₹60 lakh; professional receipts above ₹10 lakh; or TDS/TCS of ₹25,000 or more (₹50,000 for residents aged 60+).

Due dates (financial year after the tax year): 30 November where transfer pricing reports apply (s. 172); 31 October for companies, audited assessees and partners of audited firms; 31 August for non-audited business or professional income and partners of such firms; 31 July for everyone else. Business, capital gains, speculation, specified-business and race-horse losses are carried forward only if the loss return is filed by the due date; house-property loss and unabsorbed depreciation are not affected.
concepts.analogy: The due date depends on whether books are audited — salaried people file first, audited businesses later.
concepts.work: A shopkeeper with non-audited accounts files by 31 August 2027; his salaried brother by 31 July 2027.

concepts.title: Belated, revised and defective returns (s. 263(4), (5), (7))
body: Belated return (s. 263(4)): if the due date is missed, a return may still be filed by 31 December of the financial year after the tax year, or before assessment is completed, whichever is earlier.

Revised return (s. 263(5)): an original or belated return with an omission or wrong statement may be revised within 12 months from the end of the tax year (31 March 2028 for tax year 2026-27) or before assessment, whichever is earlier. A revised return can itself be revised, and a loss return can be revised too.

Defective return (s. 263(7)): if a return does not meet the prescribed requirements — for example, fields left blank or the tax audit report not filed before the return — the Assessing Officer may give 15 days (extendable) to rectify it. If not rectified, it is treated as never filed; if rectified late but before assessment, the delay may be condoned.
concepts.analogy: Belated returns fix lateness; revised returns fix mistakes; defect notices fix incompleteness.
concepts.work: A return filed on 20 July 2027 can be revised on 15 February 2028, but with a fee, because nine months have passed.

concepts.title: Updated return and additional tax (ss. 263(6), 267)
body: Section 263(6): any person may file an updated return within 48 months counted from the close of the financial year that follows the tax year, whether or not an earlier return was filed. For tax year 2026-27 the last date is 31 March 2032.

It is not allowed if it is a loss return (unless it reduces a loss shown in a loss return filed by the due date), reduces tax, creates or increases a refund, or if an updated return has already been filed for that year.

Section 267: before filing, the person pays tax and interest on the updated income plus additional tax of 25%, 50%, 60% or 70% of that tax and interest, depending on whether filing falls within 12, 24, 36 or 48 months from the end of the following financial year (the 25% band starts after the belated/revised time is over).
concepts.analogy: An updated return is a paid second chance — the longer you wait, the higher the price.
concepts.work: Filing in the third band costs 60% of the extra tax and interest on top of them.

concepts.title: Interest and fee for late filing (ss. 423, 428) and self-assessment (s. 266)
body: Section 423: simple interest at 1% per month (a part month counting as whole) from the day after the due date to the date of filing (or of assessment if no return is filed), on tax on total income less advance tax, TDS/TCS, relief u/s 157 and tax credits. Additional tax u/s 267 is excluded from the base.

Section 428: a fixed fee for filing after the due date — ₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5,00,000, otherwise ₹5,000. The same fee applies to a revised return filed more than nine months after the end of the tax year.

Section 266: tax and interest due on the return must be paid before filing. Payments are applied first to the fee, then to interest, and the balance to tax; if anything remains unpaid, the person is in default for that amount.
concepts.analogy: Lateness has two price tags: interest that grows each month and a flat fee.
concepts.work: Total income ₹4,60,000, return filed in September: the fee is ₹1,000.

concepts.title: Tax return preparers, verification, PAN and Aadhaar (ss. 262, 264, 265, 430, 467)
body: Section 264: under a notified scheme, individuals and HUFs not subject to tax audit (or audit under another law), and not companies, may file through an authorised tax return preparer.

Section 265: an individual signs his own return (a guardian or competent person if mentally incapacitated, or a power-of-attorney holder if otherwise unable); an HUF by the karta or, if absent or incapacitated, another adult member; a company by its managing director, or any director if there is none.

Section 262 governs PAN: a person who must file a return or pay tax and who meets the prescribed conditions applies for one, and PAN and Aadhaar must be quoted in specified transactions. A person eligible for Aadhaar who does not link it has his PAN made inoperative; section 430 provides a fee of up to ₹1,000 for late intimation, and section 467 a penalty of ₹10,000 for specified PAN defaults.
concepts.analogy: The right signatory makes a return valid; the right PAN makes it traceable.
concepts.work: A karta abroad for the whole of July can have his son, an adult member, sign the HUF's return.

jobs.title: Due-date calendar
jobs.situation: The firm wants a filing calendar for 40 clients.
steps: Classify each client: salaried, non-audit business, audit case, transfer pricing.
Map the due date for each class.
Flag clients with losses to carry forward.
Set reminders 15 days before each date.
jobs.takeaway: Missing the date for a loss return costs the carry-forward, not just a fee.

jobs.title: Missed income discovered late
jobs.situation: A client finds an unreported capital gain from two years ago.
steps: Check whether revision is still possible.
If not, compute tax and interest for an updated return.
Pay before filing and keep the challan.
jobs.takeaway: Act early: each passing year raises the additional-tax rate.

mcqs.q: Due date for a non-audited proprietor with business income, tax year 2026-27:
mcqs.explain: Business or professional income without a tax-audit requirement gives a due date of 31 August of the following financial year; salaried people file by 31 July. In practice: audited cases get 31 October.
mcqs.topic: Who must file and by when (s. 263(1))

mcqs.q: A resident individual under the default regime has total income of ₹3,80,000 after a deduction of ₹50,000 for employer NPS. Must she file a return?
options: Yes, because income before the deduction is ₹4,30,000
No, because total income is below ₹4,00,000
No, salaried people never need to
mcqs.explain: The test uses income before Chapter VIII deductions. ₹4,30,000 exceeds the ₹4,00,000 limit, so filing is compulsory even if rebate makes tax nil. In practice: add back deductions first.
mcqs.topic: Who must file and by when (s. 263(1))

mcqs.q: Which loss can be carried forward even if the return is filed late?
mcqs.explain: House-property loss and unabsorbed depreciation survive a late return; business, capital, speculation, specified-business and race-horse losses need the return by the due date. In practice: file loss returns on time.
mcqs.topic: Who must file and by when (s. 263(1))

mcqs.q: Last date for a belated return for tax year 2026-27 (no assessment yet):
mcqs.explain: A belated return may be filed up to 31 December of the financial year following the tax year, or before assessment, whichever is earlier. In practice: a fee applies.

mcqs.q: Mr. Aman's original return was assessed on 10 November 2027. He wants to revise it on 20 November 2027. He can:
options: Not revise it, as assessment is complete
Revise it only with the AO's approval
mcqs.explain: Revision is allowed within 12 months from the end of the tax year or before assessment is completed, whichever is earlier. Once assessed, the window closes. In practice: raise the issue in rectification or appeal instead.

mcqs.q: A belated return filed on 30 November 2027 can be revised up to:
mcqs.explain: Belated returns can also be revised, within 12 months from the end of the tax year (31 March 2028 for tax year 2026-27) or before assessment. In practice: a fee arises if revised after 31 December 2027.

mcqs.q: The time to rectify a defect notified by the Assessing Officer is ordinarily:
mcqs.explain: The AO allows 15 days from service of the intimation and can extend it if the assessee applies. An unrectified return is treated as not filed. In practice: respond promptly on the portal.

mcqs.q: An updated return is NOT allowed where it:
options: Is the first updated return for the year
mcqs.explain: It cannot reduce tax, create or increase a refund, or be a second updated return for the same year. Adding income is exactly its purpose. In practice: use the revised return to claim refunds.

mcqs.q: Additional tax on an updated return filed between 24 and 36 months after the end of the following financial year:
mcqs.explain: The bands are 25%, 50%, 60% and 70% for up to 12, 24, 36 and 48 months from the end of the financial year following the tax year. In practice: count from 31 March after the tax year's following year.

mcqs.q: Fee u/s 428 for a late return with total income of ₹4,80,000:
mcqs.explain: The fee is ₹1,000 for total income up to ₹5,00,000; above that it is ₹5,000. Lateness alone triggers it; it is not discretionary. In practice: pay it before filing.
mcqs.topic: Interest and fee for late filing (ss. 423, 428) and self-assessment (s. 266)

mcqs.q: Self-assessment payments under section 266 are applied in which order?
options: In any order the assessee chooses
mcqs.explain: The law applies amounts first towards the fee, then interest, and only the balance towards tax, so underpayment shows up as unpaid tax. In practice: compute all three before paying.
mcqs.topic: Interest and fee for late filing (ss. 423, 428) and self-assessment (s. 266)

mcqs.q: Who verifies the return of a company that has no managing director?
mcqs.explain: A company's return is verified by its managing director; where there is none, any director may verify it. In practice: check the signatory's DSC is valid.

viva.q: Which persons must file a return even with a loss or nil income?
viva.model: Companies, firms, specified institutions, and resident and ordinarily resident persons holding or benefiting from any asset or account outside India.

viva.q: What is the time limit for a revised return?
viva.model: Twelve months from the end of the tax year, or before completion of assessment, whichever is earlier; a fee applies if filed more than nine months after the year end.

viva.q: How long is the window for an updated return?
viva.model: Forty-eight months from the end of the financial year following the tax year, with additional tax rising from 25% to 70% the later it is filed.

viva.q: How is interest for late filing worked out?
viva.model: Simple interest at 1% per month, with a part month counted as a full one, from the day after the due date to the date of filing, on tax payable after advance tax, TDS, TCS and reliefs.

viva.q: Who cannot file through a tax return preparer?
viva.model: Companies and persons whose accounts must be audited under section 63 or any other law; the scheme is for other individuals and HUFs.
